title: Applied ML: Prompt Sets, Quantization Profiles, and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose:
This playbook consolidates standards and actionable procedures for: eval harness onboarding, prompt set construction and benchmarking, quantization profile guidance for model-serving, and an end-to-end regression-triage runbook. The goal is to reduce time-to-detection for degradations, increase reproducibility of evals, and provide concrete remediation paths tied to ownership and SLAs.

Scope:
- Applies to all model onboarding and performance/regression work for hosted and dedicated inference (Redwood API, Dedicated, and Private).
- Covers prompt-set design, benchmark lifecycle, quantization profile selection, and regression triage for production inference.

Owners and roles:
- Applied ML (owner): Productization of evals, prompt sets, and regression policy (Primary: Asha Patel).
- Serving Runtime (collaborator): performance impact verification and kernel-level profiling (Primary: Miguel Torres).
- SRE/Observability: alerting, dashboards, and incident escalation hooks (Primary: Leah Nguyen).
- Customer Success: triage customer-facing regressions and coordinate customer communications.

High-level workflow (summary):
1) Model onboarding -> baseline evals and prompt-set creation
2) Quantization candidate profiling and acceptance testing
3) Canary rollout with metric gates and canary dashboards
4) Continuous monitoring + automatic regression detection
5) Regression triage and root-cause remediation

1. Model Onboarding (eval harness)
Intro: The eval harness provides repeatable runs for functional correctness, safety, latency, and embedding quality. Every new model or model-variant must complete the onboarding checklist below before being promoted to production.

Onboarding checklist (required):
1. Register model in model-catalog with metadata (architecture, version, tokenizer, supported quantization formats).
2. Run baseline evals: functional test-suite, safety/toxicity suite, hallucination probe, and embedding-similarity tests.
3. Create canonical prompt-sets (see section 2) and bind them to the model entry.
4. Run quantization profile sweep (section 4) and produce a performance/quality matrix.
5. Define rollout policy (canary size, success criteria, fallback model).
6. Document owner, expected SLO impacts, and sign-off from serving-runtime and SRE.

Required outputs (artifact list):
- baseline-report: generated by eval harness (HTML/JSON)
- prompt-sets: canonical and extended lists (CSV/JSON)
- quant-profiles-report: per-profile metrics (CSV)
- rollout-policy.yaml: simple declarative rollout config

Example eval-harness run command:
$ eval-harness run --model your-model:1.0 --prompt-set canonical-core --out reports/your-model-1.0-baseline.json --profiles latency,safety,embedding

2. Prompt sets and benchmarks
Goals: Prompt sets must be representative, reproducible, and versioned. They should capture realistic user distributions and edge-cases that are critical to product quality.

Prompt-set types and guidance:
- Canonical-Core (small, fast): 200-1,000 prompts that represent the primary functionality and high-traffic use-cases. Used for quick regressions and canary checks.
- Extended-Benchmark (medium): 1,000-10,000 prompts including less-frequent edge cases and stress scenarios. Used for nightly/full-regression runs.
- Safety-and-Policy (targeted): curated prompts for toxicity, privacy leakage, PII detection, and adversarial probes.
- Latency-Distribution (synthetic): prompts constructed to exercise long-sequence and multi-turn behavior to validate memory & KV cache performance.

Design rules for a prompt-set (must follow these):
- Each prompt must include: id, seed_context, expected_behavior (short), tags (comma-separated), and difficulty label.
- Avoid dataset duplication across prompt sets; use cross-reference ids if re-used.
- Include metadata fields: source (product, synthetic, customer-safe-copy), created_at, created_by, and license.
- Maintain deterministic sampling seeds in harness runs to ensure reproducible splits.

Example prompt CSV header:
id,seed_context,expected_behavior,tags,difficulty,source,created_by,created_at
ps-0001,"Summarize the following meeting notes...","concise-summary",summarization,medium,product-example,Asha Patel,2026-09-15

Benchmarks and metrics (recommended):
- Task-level metrics: exact-match (EM), F1, BLEU or ROUGE where applicable.
- Open-generation metrics: BLEU/ROUGE, chrF, and human-like fluency scoring (when annotated).
- Safety metrics: toxicity rate (Perspective/TOX score), privacy leakage flags per 1k prompts.
- Embedding metrics: mean cosine similarity to ground-truth, retrieval-R@K for retrieval tasks.
- Latency/cost: p50/p95/p99 token latency (ms), token throughput (tokens/sec), and cost-per-1k-tokens.

Pass/fail gates (example):
- Canonical-Core: production promotion requires no regression >5% relative on primary metric and p99 latency within +20% of baseline.
- Safety: 0 new high-severity safety failures (severity defined in safety suite).

3. Quality Guardrails and Monitoring
Key guardrail metrics (table style):
Metric | Threshold | Alert level | Owner
---|---:|---|---
Primary-task-metric (task-specific) | >5% relative drop vs baseline | P1 incident | applied-ml
Safety-high-severity-rate | any new high-severity event | P0 immediate | security-and-compliance
Embedding-similarity-mean | >0.07 absolute drop | P1 | applied-ml
p99-token-latency | >+50% vs baseline | P2 | eng-serving-runtime
Model-error-rate (500/4xx on API) | >1% | P1 | eng-sre

Automated monitors and dashboards (required):
- Canary dashboard: per-canary-run metrics, diffs vs baseline, sample outputs (first 20 failures).
- Nightly regression job: runs Extended-Benchmark and posts a report to the eval reports bucket and creates a regression ticket if gates fail.
- Safety monitor: near real-time safety scoring on a 1% traffic sample; raises paged alerts for new high-severity patterns.

Escalation matrix (short):
1) Alert triggers nightly-regression ticket (automated).
2) Applied-ML triage within 2 business hours for non-severity incidents.
3) For P0 safety events, security-and-compliance is paged immediately.
4) If production impact observed, SRE performs rollback/cutover to last known-good model.

4. Quantization Profiles and Acceptance Testing
Decision framework: Quantize only when the expected cost/throughput gains outweigh quality delta and there is a tested fallback. Quantization runs are split into: research-sweep, candidate-acceptance, and production-rollout.

Minimum acceptance testing for profiles:
- Run the Canonical-Core and Safety suites end-to-end.
- Measure delta on primary task metric and safety metrics; delta must be below defined thresholds.
- Run latency and memory profiling on target GPU types and validate KV cache correctness.
- Run full determinism check: top-k/top-p sampling and seed reproducibility for deterministic outputs where required.

Recommended quantization profiles (example table):
Profile name | Bits | Typical throughput uplift | Use cases | Acceptance gate
---|---:|---:|---|---
q8_0 (baseline) | 8-bit (symmetric)| 1.8x | interactive chat, latency-sensitive | <= 1.5% primary metric drop, no safety regression
q4_c (aggressive) | 4-bit (compressed) | 2.6x | throughput-first, batch embeddings | <= 3% metric drop, manual review required
fp16 (mixed) | 16-bit | 1.1x | compatibility and lower-variance outputs | baseline for comparison

Quantization checklist (candidate):
1. Produce quant-profiles-report CSV with columns: profile, metric_name, baseline_value, candidate_value, delta_pct, run_id.
2. Perf-run: measure cold-start memory, warm throughput, and p99 inference time.
3. Safety-run: run safety suite and manual review for flagged examples.
4. Sign-off: applied-ml + serving-runtime approve before canary.

Sample quant-profiles-report CSV header:
profile,metric,baseline_value,candidate_value,delta_pct,run_id
q8_0,task_f1,0.842,0.835,-0.83,run-2028-02-27-1

5. Regression Triage Playbook (detailed)
When a regression is detected (automated or customer-reported), follow the steps below. Triage must be time-boxed to accelerate mitigation.

Initial detection (0-30 minutes):
1. Confirm alert and scope: check canary dashboard, production-sampled logs, and recent deployment activity.
2. Capture failure samples: store the first 100 failing prompts and model outputs to the triage bucket.
3. Determine if regression matches known-change window (deployments, infra changes, kernel updates, quantization pushes).

Triage (30-180 minutes):
1. Reproduce locally: run eval-harness with the canonical-core prompt set against the reported model version and last-known-good model.
2. Diff outputs using the harness diff tool: eval-harness diff --base last-known-good.json --candidate candidate.json --out diffs/report.html
3. Classify the regression: quality (task metric), safety, latency/cost, or infra (errors/500s).
4. If safety: page security-and-compliance and follow immediate response (P0).
5. If quality and reproducible: create issue in model-regressions board with reproducible recipe and attach sample failures.

Mitigation (2-8 hours):
- Short-term: rollback to last-known-good model or reduce traffic weight to canary model.
- Mid-term: revert quantization or change sampling parameters (top-k/top-p) that introduced variance.
- Long-term: schedule model retrain or prompt-set augmentation and new canary cycle.

Post-incident (8 hours-2 weeks):
1. Root cause analysis (RCA): include diffs, profiling traces, quantization artifacts, and kernel logs.
2. Postmortem: produce an incident postmortem with action items and owners.
3. Update prompt-sets and eval harness tests to catch this class of regression in the future.

Triage checklist (artifact requirements):
- reproducer.yaml: minimal steps to reproduce using eval-harness
- failure-samples.zip: the first 100 failing requests + expected behavior notes
- perf-traces.json: profiler output from serving runtime if latency-related
- sign-off: rollback or remediation owner listed

6. Reporting and Continuous Improvement
- Nightly runs: Extended-Benchmark push report to reports bucket and create Slack summary in #applied-ml-regressions.
- Monthly health check: applied-ml publishes a model-health report covering top regressions, quantization rollouts, and safety incidents.
- Lessons-learned: update prompt-set suites and quantization rules based on RCA outcomes.

Appendices
A. Templates (copy into eval-harness/templates):
- reproducer.yaml example:
  model: model-name:1.0
  prompt_set: canonical-core
  seed: 42
  samples: 200
  deterministic: true

B. Example rollout-policy.yaml:
  canary:
    weight: 10
    duration_minutes: 60
    success_criteria:
      primary_metric_delta_pct: -2
      p99_latency_pct: 20
    fallback: last-known-good

C. Useful commands:
- Run canonical: eval-harness run --model $MODEL --prompt-set canonical-core --out reports/$MODEL.json
- Diff two runs: eval-harness diff --base reports/last-known-good.json --candidate reports/$MODEL.json --out diffs/$MODEL.html
- Run quant sweep: eval-harness quant-sweep --model $MODEL --profiles q8_0,q4_c --out reports/quant-$MODEL.csv
